collection.description: A landslip in the hills has uncovered a hot spring, steaming in a hollow of black rock.

ask.text:
A landslip in the hills has uncovered a hot spring, steaming in a hollow of black rock. The water is cloudy white and smells faintly of eggs. One of the elders says (his/her) grandmother bathed in a spring like this when she was young, and came out "looking like her own daughter," but that her sister came out looking like their grandmother.
(Name) has a stiff back and a long day behind (him/her), and the water looks very, very warm.
Should (name) get all the way in, or just soak (his/her) feet?

c1o1.text: When (name) climbs out, pink and sleepy, (his/her) face feels tight. In the still water at the edge, an older face looks back at (him/her): grey at the temples, deep lines round the eyes. (He/She) feels exactly the same, only more relaxed than in years. "Well," (he/she) says, "my back's better." The elder who told the story nods slowly. "The sister was very happy too," (he/she) says.

c1o2.text: When (name) climbs out, (his/her) face looks the way it did years ago, smooth and bright, as though (he/she) has slept for a month. The next day, there's a queue at the hot spring. The day after that, there's a second queue of people who came out looking older and are cross about it. The elders decide the spring should only be used on special occasions.

c1.text: (Name) sinks into the cloudy water up to (his/her) chin and groans. The heat goes straight into (his/her) bones. The steam is so thick (he/she) can't see the rocks at the edge...

c2o1.text: (Name) breathes in the steam, and breathes it out, and by the time (he/she) pulls (his/her) feet out, wrinkled as dried fruit, (his/her) face has changed. Younger. Brighter. "It was just my feet," (he/she) keeps saying, at home, staring into a water bowl. "It was only ever my feet."

c2o2.text: (Name) has had a cough for weeks. Sitting in the steam, it loosens, and (he/she) coughs up something unpleasant into the bushes and then sits back, breathing freely for the first time in a long while. The healers come up the next day with baskets, and start bottling the water, and arguing about how much.

c2.text: (Name) sits on the black rock and lowers (his/her) feet into the water. It's like being hugged by the ground. A cool breeze blows the steam into (his/her) face...
